summary:
AstraHealth is an offline-first health monitoring and self-assessment app for astronauts on ISS, Moon and Mars missions. It combines simulated wearable and body-scan readings, short daily, weekly and monthly check-ins, skin and injury photos, and uploaded lab files into one health record. It colours every measurement Normal, Watch or Alert using rules drawn from NASA and Canadian Space Agency sources and adjusted for spaceflight: in-flight blood pressure, temperature after 60 days in microgravity, low-pressure habitats. An AI medical briefing explains the last check-in, the last 24 hours and the 7-day trends in plain language, with precise care steps. If a situation looks too serious, AstraHealth gives interim first aid and starts a cancellable SOS to the ground medical lab and the ISS. It also shows how long the signal will take to arrive.

This matters because the further crews travel, the less they can rely on a doctor on Earth. On Mars a message can take 20 minutes each way, so astronauts must spot problems early and act on their own. AstraHealth keeps working with no Earth link and no AI, using deterministic, reviewable rules.
details: AstraHealth is an offline-first spaceflight health companion that monitors six key vitals, runs body scans, tracks NASA-scheduled daily, weekly, and monthly check-ins, and displays rotating 3D organs alongside trend drift warnings ("reaches Watch in about N days") and local medical records. Designed for deep-space autonomy, it adapts safety thresholds to the mission timeline (transit, orbit, or surface) and Earth communication delays—prompting flight surgeon contact near Earth while guiding immediate self-care on Mars—and includes an "Is it me or the air?" check linking symptoms to cabin CO2, plus an automatic SOS with a 30-second cancel window for life-threatening signs. By detecting subtle issues like sleep disruption, infections, or radiation exposure early while keeping personal journals strictly on-device, it empowers astronauts with clear self-care steps and minimizes alert fatigue through single-issue alerts and quiet re-checks. Built with TypeScript, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Recharts, Three.js, IndexedDB, Python (with NumPy/SciPy for generating 3D models from reference images), Playwright, and an optional Google Gemini API layer, the app runs in any modern browser on a laptop or tablet without specialized hardware. In designing AstraHealth, we prioritized crew safety—ensuring deterministic rules set alert statuses so the AI can explain or raise concerns without ever hiding one—alongside communication blackouts, data privacy, microgravity usability with large touch targets and 1–5 scales, accessible plain language, and a clear decision-support disclaimer.
